title: arXiv AI — Monday, 16 November 2026 — 5 notable recent papers
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; the ordering is inferred from checkable attention and quality signals, and citation evidence is limited for very recent papers.

sections.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
sections.abstract: The authors train an open-weight 27B reasoning model with robot-use reinforcement learning entirely in simulation and report transfer to unseen tasks, a new robot, and real hardware, including 60% success across their real dual-arm robot trials.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce PEAR and robot-use reinforcement learning, reporting that simulation-only training lets the model control real robots without demonstrations or a task-specific harness.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say training covered only two simulators and a small task set; long reasoning and prompt dependence remain practical limitations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Independent paper notes by Lixin Xu and coverage by AREX discuss the simulation-to-real result; public project/code site and cs.RO/cs.LG cross-list are supporting signals.

sections.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a reproducible benchmark of 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applications that evaluates agents using text, vision, audio, and video, and report a best task-success rate of 62.3% for the tested systems.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a human-validated, container-isolated benchmark intended to make diverse multimodal web-agent evaluation more reproducible.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that audio/video interaction is limited to prerecorded audio and discrete video frames; model-versus-harness comparisons also do not fully control resource use.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations & Datasets Track and listed on NeurIPS and OpenReview; it spans three core AI categories and has a public benchmark site.

sections.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a 42-task benchmark for testing whether language models can inspect, repair, write, reject impossible edits to, and compress neural-network weights without gradient descent; results show current strengths on small networks and substantial gaps on larger-model editing and compression.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define and operationalize Weight-Space Programming as a benchmarked capability across five task tracks, with metered execution and constrained edits.
sections.unique_caveat: Reliable patching of language models and data-free compression are not demonstrated in the authors' results; GPT-6.1-Sol was evaluated on 38 rather than all 42 tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Independent coverage appeared at CASRAI and DEV Community; public task registry, sandbox harness, leaderboard, and cs.LG/cs.AI cross-list support relevance.

sections.title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents
sections.abstract: The authors combine verified hierarchical planning with runtime enforcement so an LLM agent can block policy-violating tool calls while using its verified plan to recover, reporting 1.7× the average task success of the strongest baselines with no specification violations on their benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose checking an agent's structured plan against formal specifications before tool use, then using runtime enforcement and the plan to guide recovery after a blocked action.
sections.unique_caveat: Specifications still require manual validation, tool contracts must accurately describe tool behavior, and automated theorem provers may not complete verification in practice.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Listed as a NeurIPS 2026 Oral and has a Princeton-hosted paper and poster; venue selection and public technical materials are the principal signals.

sections.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
sections.abstract: The authors adapt automatic-speech-recognition models for intracortical brain-to-text decoding, reporting a 4.39% word error rate on publicly available data and mobile-device throughput up to 370× real time.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report an end-to-end portable decoding framework with adaptation to neural non-stationarity and gradient-based saliency maps that align with physiological priors.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evaluation uses publicly available data from one intracortical speech-neuroprosthesis user, so performance across users and longer-term deployments remains unestablished here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Listed as a NeurIPS 2026 paper/poster and covered by DeekoyaAI and OpenTrain; cs.LG cross-list and mobile deployment are supporting signals.
